# Admission Representatives — brief

**Output:** `pages/admission-representatives/index.html`, `search.html`, and `<slug>.html`
**Source:** https://admissions.umd.edu/admission-representatives (captured 2026-08-31)
**Generated by:** `scripts/build-representatives.py` from `briefs/representatives-data.json`

## Why this page exists

The source page is a 24-person directory where **each rep's bio opens in a
modal**. The design system has no modal component, and nothing in it projects
an arbitrary content payload over the page. So the central question this
recreation answers is: what do the bios become instead?

They become **pages**. `umd-element-person-hero` is described in
`registry-person.json` as "a hero-scale individual feature for a person profile
landing page" and carries its own `breadcrumb` slot — it is built for exactly
this. Each rep gets a real URL, which is strictly better than the modal: the
bios are linkable, shareable and back-button-able, and the territory list stops
being something you can only find by clicking a photo.

## Section order

### Landing page (`index.html`)

| # | Section | Component |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Hero | `umd-element-hero data-layout-height="small" data-layout-text="center"` |
| 2 | We're Here for You | `.reps-intro-*` eyebrow lockup + brand chevron |
| 3 | Meet the Office | `umd-element-section-intro include-separator` + `umd-layout-grid-border-four` × 24 `umd-element-person` |
| 4 | Join the Mailing List | `umd-element-banner-promo` |

Section 2 is the treatment already used on `pages/how-to-apply/index.html` and
`pages/tuition/index.html`: rule, uppercase eyebrow, rich text, with
`umd-element-brand-logo-animation` riding behind it and overlapping ~180px up
into the hero.

Section 3's `include-separator` draws the DS's red vertical accent above the
headline. It is a **boolean** attribute, and the component renders it as a
`::before` on `.intro-default-container` (2px × 64px, `#E21833`, centred, with
80px of top padding) — not as a DOM node, which makes it easy to look for in
the wrong place and conclude it is unimplemented.

### Bio page (`<slug>.html`)

| # | Section | Component |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Profile | `umd-element-person-hero` (owns the breadcrumb and the only contact action) |
| 2 | Favorite Maryland Moment | eyebrow lockup + rich text — **omitted if the rep has no bio** |
| 3 | Territories | `.umd-admissions-representative-regions-list` — **omitted if the rep has no regions** |
| 4 | Back to directory | `umd-element-call-to-action data-display="secondary"` |

### Search page (`search.html`) — an alternative to the index

A second presentation of the same 24 reps, modelled on the CMS's out-of-the-box
**person index** template (`omc.umd.edu/people`) rather than on a static grid.

| # | Section | Component |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Hero | identical to `index.html` — same image, copy, centred small variant |
| 2 | Filter | DS highlight panel: territory `<select>` + search input + submit |
| 3 | Results | `umd-layout-grid-border-four` — **the same cards as the index** |
| 4 | Load More | `button.umd-action-outline`, page size 8 |
| 5 | We're Here for You | the index's intro copy, **moved to the foot of the page** |
| 6 | Join the Mailing List | `umd-element-banner-promo` |

**The rich text moves to the bottom.** The CMS person-index template has no
rich-text region above the filter, so on this page the copy cannot lead. Below
the results it still answers "how do I actually reach these people". The brand
chevron does **not** come with it: on `index.html` that animation is positioned
to overlap ~180px *up* into the hero above it, and at the foot of the page it
has nothing to bite into and would ride over the results grid instead.

**Almost none of the template needed reproducing.** Measured against our loaded
bundles, the DS classes the CMS template uses are nearly all present:
`umd-layout-background-highlight-light` (the grey panel and its red left rule),
`umd-layout-grid-gap-stacked` / `-two`, `umd-layout-grid-inline-stretch`,
`umd-text-line-trailing-light`, `umd-field-select-wrapper`, `umd-field-input`,
`umd-action-outline`, `umd-skip-content`, `sr-only`. Only two families are
missing, and those are page CSS §26:

- the `umd-shell-*` classes — shellcraft *site* CSS, not the design system
- the Tailwind utilities the template leans on for the search row (`flex`,
  `gap-min`, `items-center`, `aspect-square`, `bg-red`, `h-[44px]`)

`briefs/experts-filter.md` already documents that same 44×44 search bar in
"minimal lift" form; that is what §26 uses.

**Territories are grouped.** 56 of them across 24 reps, and all but one
(Montgomery County) belong to exactly one person. A flat 56-item `<select>` is a
lot to scroll, and the data carries its own grouping — `Maryland - Kent County`,
`New York - Upstate`. Splitting on `" - "` yields `<optgroup>`s for Maryland
(25), New York (6), New Jersey (3), Virginia (3) and Pennsylvania (2); a lone
`X - Y` is not worth a group of one and folds back into a trailing "States &
Regions" group with the 17 unprefixed entries.

**No "Please select a valid option." error line.** The CMS template has one
because its dropdown is populated from a taxonomy that can go stale. Ours is
generated from the same JSON that renders the cards, so an invalid option
cannot occur.

**Filtering is client-side over the server-rendered cards**, the same shape as
the UMD experts controller (`briefs/experts-filter.md`): AND across the two
dimensions, a plain lowercase substring test for the text against a precomputed
`data-search` index (name + title + territories), and Load More as paging of
the already-filtered array. No network at any point.

Two things that are easy to get wrong here:

- **The script builds fresh cards; it never moves the originals.**
  `umd-element-person` re-renders *additively* when it reconnects — detach a
  card and re-attach it and its shadow root ends up with two `.person-block`s,
  so it draws the same person twice at double height (389px → 694px, measured).
  `replaceChildren` re-inserts the cards already on screen, so one Load More
  click did that to every visible card and the grid appeared to repeat its rows.
  The controller captures each card's `outerHTML` at init and builds new
  elements from it, and Load More only ever **appends the delta**. Hiding
  non-matches with `display: none` is not the alternative: `layout.min.css`
  draws the grid's top border with `:nth-child(1..4)`, which counts DOM
  position, so filtering out the first four cards strands the border on hidden
  cells. Full write-up in `OVERRIDES.md`.
- **Shadow injections on this page must be re-runnable.** Cards built after load
  never saw the one-shot `customElements.whenDefined()` pass, so the
  `a.person-name` hover injection is exposed as `window.umdInjectPersonLinkCss()`
  (guarded per element) and called after every append.
- **`grid-animations.js` is deliberately absent.** The canonical script animates
  grid children in on reveal; here the children are replaced on every keystroke,
  so every filter would re-trigger the entry animation and the results would
  flicker. `index.html` still loads it.

The form ships with `hidden` and the script reveals it, so with JS off the page
degrades to all 24 cards and no dead controls.

**The 80px under the grid lives on the grid's wrapper, not on either follower.**
The DS vertical-rhythm classes are margin-**bottom** only — measured,
`umd-layout-vertical-landing` is `margin-bottom: 120px; margin-top: 0`, the same
thing `CLAUDE.md` notes about `-child`. The grid's wrapper is a bare
`umd-layout-space-horizontal-larger` with no vertical class, so nothing
separated it from what came next and both the Load More button and the trailing
copy sat flush against the last row of cards. Putting the gap on the wrapper is
what makes it hold in every state: Load More is `display: none` once all matches
are shown, so a margin on that section would disappear with it and the copy
would jump back against the grid the moment a filter narrowed the results.
Verified at 80px in all four states — default, all-shown, filtered, and
no-matches (where the empty message takes the grid's place).

## Which reps have pages, and why only six

`briefs/representatives-data.json` holds **all 24 reps** — every name, title,
headshot, bio and territory list. Six carry `"page": true`. They were picked to
cover every shape the bio template has to survive, not by seniority:

| Rep | What it exercises |
|---|---|
| Abigail Trice | bio + 9 territories (the longest list) |
| Ebony Freeman | bio + 2 territories (the common case) |
| Nico Magpantay | bio + 4 territories (the longest bio paragraph) |
| Taylor Duvall | bio, no territories, and a 100-character job title |
| Sofia Cisneros | territories, **no** bio — section 2 must disappear |
| James B. Massey, Jr. | **neither** — page collapses to hero + back link |

**Adding the other eighteen is a data edit:** flip `"page"` to `true` and re-run
`python3 scripts/build-representatives.py`. No code change.

### The known consequence of stopping at six

`umd-element-person` renders `<a slot="name">` and `<p slot="name">`
**identically** — same `.person-name.umd-sans-larger`, same black, same 700
weight, no underline (measured against `cdn.js@1.18.12`). That is correct for
the finished page, where all 24 link and the grid is uniform. In the interim it
means the eighteen unlinked names look clickable and are not.

The page mitigates this with a shadow injection that underlines and reddens
`a.person-name` on hover/focus, so the six that work announce themselves. It
does not fully solve the resting state — that resolves by generating the rest.

## Content decisions

- **"Click on their photo" is rewritten.** The source's instruction —
  *"Learn more about each of our reps, and their territories, by clicking on
  their photo"* — describes the modal. It becomes *"…and the territories they
  cover, on their profile pages."*
- **No individual email addresses.** The source publishes none; it asks readers
  to email `ApplyMaryland@umd.edu` with their city and state in the subject.
  Each bio page keeps that single address but prefills the subject with the
  rep's name (`?subject=Student Inquiry for <name>`), which is the same routing
  instruction the source gives in prose.
- **One contact action, not two.** The `email` slot and a `slot="actions"` CTA
  both pointed at the same `mailto:`, so the button restated the link directly
  above it. The CTA is gone and the email link reads **"Email &lt;first name&gt;"**
  rather than the raw address — its `aria-label` still names the actual inbox,
  so the destination is not lost for a screen reader.
- **Breadcrumb kept, unlike every other page in this project.** Not a
  reversal of the "no breadcrumb" decision in `prospective-students.md`: the
  bio pages do not add `umd-element-breadcrumb`, they fill the `breadcrumb`
  slot that `umd-element-person-hero` already renders. Leaving it empty leaves
  a gap in the component's own layout.
- **Sofia Cisneros' bio headline is dropped.** Her CMS entry labels its only
  headline "Regions" — the field is reused — with no bio behind it. Rendering
  it would have produced a heading over nothing.
- **`&nbsp;` and stray `<br>` stripped** from the CMS bio text; several entries
  carry them mid-sentence from the source editor.

## Two component findings

Both are recorded in `OVERRIDES.md`.

1. **`umd-element-person-hero` silently drops `slot="association"`.**
   `registry-person.json` lists it, but the component rebuilds its text lockup
   from the light DOM reading only `name` and `job-title`. The unit name would
   have been dead markup, so it is not emitted.
2. **The `breadcrumb` slot validates, and the registry's example markup for it
   is wrong.** The slot only accepts a `umd-element-breadcrumb` — anything else
   logs `Slot "breadcrumb" contains invalid elements` and renders unstyled
   light-DOM links. And `registry-navigation.json` shows `slot="paths"` as an
   `<ol>` of `<li>`s, which silently breaks the separators: the DS draws them
   with `.breadcrumb-path + *::before`, so the paths must be adjacent siblings.
   `RULES.md` § "Breadcrumb" has the correct form — flat `<a>` siblings in a
   `<div slot="paths">`, current page as a `<p>` — and outranks the registry.
   Done right it needs **no page CSS**.

## Section placement

`pages/admission-representatives/` is its own section directory, matching the
source URL. It has no `data-child-ref` group in `shared/header.html`, so the
mobile drawer opens at its top level — the same correct-for-now state as
`pages/calendar/` and `pages/personas/`. If a `Connect` section later earns a
nav item, this moves under it and the drawer refs follow the directory name.

## Images

All 24 headshots are the source page's own, pulled at 620×620 (its display
size) into `images/admission-representatives/<slug>.jpg` — 760KB for the set,
none over 56KB.

| Slot | File | Origin |
|---|---|---|
| Hero | `images/admission-representatives/representatives-hero.jpg` | source page (1440×544, used as-is) |
| Cards / profiles | `images/admission-representatives/<slug>.jpg` | source page (620×620 each) |
